endorsements.quote: Notwithstanding, it is important to note that improvement in prediction does not necessarily mean improvement in clinical care, and outcomes should be measurable and evaluated using scientific approaches.
However, patients also deserve clear communication about the use of these technologies, their benefits, and risks.

unlisted_practices: Update AI models routinely to incorporate clinical guidelines, new data, and changing patient populations.
Establish robust quality control processes to ensure consistent AI performance and detect errors.
Develop standardized protocols for AI model maintenance and validation.
Implement institutional guidelines defining acceptable AI use and attribution methods in medical education, including AI awareness in academic integrity training.
Have attending physicians review and contextualize AI-generated educational summaries and journal club discussion points to confirm validity and relevance.
Test AI-based clinical decision support tools in both primary care and nephrology settings.
Consider the potential adverse effects of AI adoption on labor demand and administrative roles.

screen.reason: Official statement/framework paper from the American Society of Nephrology providing principles and guidance for responsible AI deployment and governance in kidney care.
